role.q: How do you gather requirements for a new project?
role.why: The core of the BA job.
role.model: I identify the stakeholders and their goals, then run interviews and workshops starting from the current process and its pain points. I observe users when possible, collect examples and volumes, and write the needs as user stories with acceptance criteria. I validate them with the stakeholders and prioritise with the Product Owner using MoSCoW.

role.q: Two stakeholders ask for conflicting requirements. What do you do?
role.why: Conflict management is daily for a BA.
role.model: I make the conflict explicit and bring facts: the goal behind each request, the users impacted, cost and risk. Often a solution covers both needs. If not, I present the options to the person who owns the decision, usually the Product Owner or the sponsor, with a recommendation, and I document the decision.

role.q: Write a user story with acceptance criteria for a password reset.
role.model: As a registered user, I want to reset my password by email, so that I can access my account if I forget it. Given I have an account, when I request a reset, then I receive a link valid for one hour. Given the link has expired, when I open it, then I can request a new one. Given an unknown email, when I request a reset, then I see the same confirmation message, so accounts are not disclosed.

role.q: How do you know a requirement is good enough for developers?
role.model: It is clear, testable and small enough: it follows INVEST, has acceptance criteria covering the main and error cases, includes examples or mock-ups when the UI matters, and has no open questions. With the team we agree a Definition of Ready and review stories in refinement before planning.

role.why: Process thinking is a key BA value.
role.model: Customer refunds took 9 days because requests went through three teams by email. I mapped the as-is process in BPMN with the teams, found two approvals that never rejected anything and data typed twice. The to-be process removed one approval and used a single form linked to the order. Refunds dropped to 3 days.

role.q: How do you prepare and run a UAT?
role.model: I write test cases from the acceptance criteria, prepare test data and the environment, and select testers from the business. During UAT I follow progress daily, triage defects with the team by severity, and report. At the end, I present the results against the agreed exit criteria so the business can decide go or no-go.

role.q: What is the difference between a BA and a Product Owner?
role.why: Checks you understand your role in agile teams.
role.model: The Product Owner owns the product's value and the backlog order, and makes the final prioritisation decisions. The BA analyses needs and processes in depth, writes and details requirements, and supports the team and the PO. In small teams one person can do both.

role.q: How do you use data in your work as a BA?
role.why: Many BA offers ask for SQL and Power BI.
role.model: I use SQL and dashboards to size problems and prioritise: how many customers are affected, how often, what it costs. I check assumptions before workshops, define how we will measure success after release, and verify the results afterwards.
